page: Microsoft Azure M16bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration delivers 16 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, clocked at up to 4.0 GHz. The processor provides 105 MB of L3 cache alongside modern instruction set extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is fixed at 128.0 GB, producing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The virtual machine includes no local storage or attached GPUs, requiring reliance on remote block storage with support for Premium Storage tiers.

Benchmark measurements reveal strong single-thread throughput alongside standard multi-core efficiency. Geekbench single-core execution reached 2213.0, aligning with top-quartile results and corroborated by single-threaded gzip compression at 32.93 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.73 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is balanced, with PassMark CPU scoring 27919.15 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 108.6 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth measured 108.38 GB/sec and 67.71 GB/sec, respectively. In inference testing with a small 135M parameter language model, text generation attained 333.36 tokens per second, reflecting benefits from the AMX matrix acceleration units.

The 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers favorable cost efficiency for memory-constrained workloads by reducing the number of compute cores required to maintain high memory allocations. A primary operational tradeoff is the total lack of bundled local NVMe storage, which makes storage performance dependent on network block storage sizing and throughput limits. The M16bs_v3 is suited for production relational database hosting, in-memory caching solutions like Redis, ETL data transformation jobs, and small-model CPU inference pipelines.
